subtopics.title: Inside the Atom — Protons, Neutrons and Electrons

questions.question: The gold-foil experiment showed that an atom's mass and positive charge are:
options: Spread evenly through the whole atom
Concentrated in a tiny central nucleus, with mostly empty space around it

questions.question: The charges of the proton, neutron and electron are, in order:
The electron's mass is ignored when adding up an atom's mass because it is:
options: About one two-thousandth of a proton's mass — negligible next to the nucleus

questions.question: A neutral atom always has:
options: Equal numbers of protons and neutrons
Equal numbers of protons and electrons

subtopics.title: Atomic Number, Mass Number, Notation and Ions

questions.question: The atomic number Z counts the:
options: Protons in the nucleus — the element's identity

questions.question: Sodium twenty-three has Z = 11 and A = 23. Its neutron count is:
In element notation, the mass number and atomic number are written:
options: A as a superscript and Z as a subscript, both to the left of the symbol
Both to the right of the symbol
A below and Z above, to the right
Only the mass number is ever written

questions.question: A calcium ion with a charge of two plus has 20 protons and:
options: 18 electrons — a two-plus charge means two electrons were lost

questions.question: Isotopes of an element have:
options: The same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons
Different numbers of electrons in the neutral atom

questions.question: Chlorine thirty-five and chlorine thirty-seven both have 17 protons. Their neutron counts are:
options: 18 and 20 — A minus Z for each

questions.question: With 75% chlorine-35 and 25% chlorine-37, the relative atomic mass is:
Isotopes of the same element are chemically identical because they have:
options: The same electron arrangement — chemistry is run by the electrons, and neutrons carry no charge

subtopics.title: Energy Levels, Orbitals and Electron Configuration

questions.question: An orbital is:
options: The path an electron orbits along, like a planet
A region of space where an electron is most likely to be found, holding at most two electrons
A level that holds exactly eight electrons

questions.question: The filling order of orbitals up to Z = 20 is:
The sp notation for chlorine, with 17 electrons, is:
In an Aufbau diagram, a pair of electrons in one orbital is drawn as:
options: Two arrows in the same direction
Two dots side by side in separate orbitals
One arrow up and one arrow down — opposite spins

questions.question: In the stadium picture, the pea on the centre spot stands for:
options: The nucleus — nearly all the mass and all the positive charge in a tiny space

questions.question: The electrons stay near the nucleus because:
options: They are locked in place and cannot move
Opposite charges attract — the positive nucleus pulls the negative electrons

questions.question: In the gold-foil experiment, the rare particles that bounced back showed that:
options: Something tiny, dense and charged sits at the atom's centre

questions.question: In the twins picture, the heavier backpack stands for:
options: Extra neutrons — more mass, same identity and same chemistry

questions.question: No chlorine atom weighs 35,5 because 35,5 is:
options: The weighted average of a crowd of isotopes — three light atoms for every heavy one
A printing error on the table
The mass of chlorine's neutrons alone

questions.question: The average 35,5 sits much closer to 35 than to 37 because:
options: The heavier isotope is more common
The lighter isotope is more common — the average leans toward the bigger share

subtopics.title: Filling the Hotel From the Ground Floor

questions.question: The three house rules of the electron hotel are:
options: Fill from the top; three per room; pairs spin together
Fill the p rooms first; two per room; never pair
Fill cheapest rooms first; at most two per room with opposite spins; spread out singly in equal p rooms before pairing
One electron per floor; roommates spin together; skip floor 3

questions.question: Sodium's 11 electrons check in as:
The quick self-check on any sp notation is:
options: The notation must end in p six
The first number must equal the last
The superscripts must add up to the atomic number
